Zobah
ZOH-bah
proper noun
Hebrew tsōbāh, Aram-zobah, a Syrian kingdom north of Damascus, the realm of Hadadezer the son of Rehob, whom Saul fought and David subdued.

📖 Biblical Definition

Zobah, called also Aram-zobah, was a Syrian kingdom lying north of Damascus, a power of the heathen against which the kings of Israel waged war. Saul in his day fought against the kings of Zobah among all his enemies on every side, and whithersoever he turned himself he vexed them (1Sa 14:47). But it was David who broke their strength, for he smote Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates (2Sa 8:3), and took from him chariots and horsemen and footmen, and put garrisons among the Syrians of Damascus, so that the Syrians became servants to David and brought gifts; and the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went (2Sa 8:6). When the children of Ammon afterward hired the Syrians of Zoba against him, these too were beaten down (2Sa 10:6). David dedicated unto the LORD the silver and gold he won of Zobah, with the spoil of all the nations he subdued (2Sa 8:11-12); and the title of the sixtieth Psalm remembers his striving with Aram-zobah. The dictionary honours that here the LORD subdued the heathen under His anointed king, a figure of the greater Son of David who shall put all enemies under His feet. The believer is taught that through God we shall do valiantly, for He it is that shall tread down our enemies (Psa 60:12), and that every spoil of every victory belongs of right to the LORD.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A Syrian kingdom north of Damascus, realm of Hadadezer, fought by Saul and subdued by David, who dedicated its spoil to the LORD.

expand to see more

ZOBAH, called also Aram-zobah, a Syrian kingdom lying north of Damascus.

It was the realm of Hadadezer the son of Rehob.

Saul fought against the kings of Zobah, and David smote and subdued them.

David put garrisons in Syria and dedicated the spoil of Zobah unto the LORD.

It witnesses to the LORD subduing the heathen under His anointed king.

📖 Key Scripture

2Sa 8:3 — "David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates."

1Sa 14:47 — "So Saul took the kingdom over Israel, and fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines: and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them."

2Sa 8:6 — "Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought gifts. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went."

Psa 60:12 — "Through God we shall do valiantly: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A kingdom of the heathen subdued under David; it witnesses to the LORD treading down the nations under His anointed king.

expand to see more

Zobah is a kingdom of the sacred record, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader of Samuel and the Psalms may know it for a real Syrian realm, the power of Hadadezer that Saul fought and David subdued, whose spoil was dedicated unto the LORD.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the LORD subdues the heathen under His anointed king, and that the victory and the spoil are His. David smote Zobah and laid up its silver and gold for the house of God, a figure of the greater Son of David who shall put all His enemies under His feet. The believer is taught that through God we shall do valiantly, for He it is that shall tread down our enemies, and that to Him belongs every spoil of every triumph.
